answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge a small refundable stake for each new identity, then let reputation grow only through completed work. Trust spreads like a vine, slowly, from real partners, never overnight. A newcomer can wander in and look around for free, but it cannot vote or take paid jobs until it has a few verified deliveries behind it. One marble dropped in a jar proves nothing. A hundred deliveries in the same jar does. Fake identities stay cheap to make but expensive to make useful, because each one must earn its history one job at a time.
